title: Channels, Kraus, Choi, and Stinespring Representations

items.title: Finite Kraus representation
items.statement:
Let $H$ and $K$ be finite-dimensional (have finite bases by [[def-dimension]])
complex inner-product spaces ([[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]),
with the root convention that
each inner product is linear in its first argument. Write $\mathcal L(H)$ for
the complex-linear endomorphisms of $H$ and $\mathcal L(H,K)$ for the
complex-linear maps from $H$ to $K$ ([[def-linear-map]]). A **finite Kraus
representation** of a complex-linear map
$\Phi:\mathcal L(H)\to\mathcal L(K)$ is a finite family
$(K_a)_{a\in A}\subseteq\mathcal L(H,K)$ such that

$$\Phi(X)=\sum_{a\in A}K_a X K_a^\dagger\qquad\text{for every }X\in\mathcal L(H),$$

where $K_a^\dagger:K\to H$ is the adjoint
([[def-adjoint-of-a-linear-map-between-inner-product-spaces]]), which exists
uniquely in finite dimensions ([[thm-adjoint-exists-and-is-unique-in-finite-dimension]]).
The composition $K_a\circ X\circ K_a^\dagger$ maps $K$ to $K$, so the sum
defines an output endomorphism for each input endomorphism $X$. The index set
$A$ may be empty; its sum is then the zero map. Zero operators are allowed in
a nonempty family.
proof_obligations: Specify the input endomorphism and output rectangular operators/adjoints.
Define empty and zero-operator families without asserting complete positivity.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information (2018), §2.2.2
John Preskill, Quantum Computation, Chapter 3, §3.2.1

items.title: Finite-dimensional linear isometries satisfy the adjoint identity
items.statement:
Let $H,K$ be finite-dimensional (have finite bases by [[def-dimension]])
complex inner-product spaces and let
$V:H\to K$ be a linear isometry. Then $V^\dagger V=I_H$. If $V$ is also
surjective, then $VV^\dagger=I_K$.
proof_obligations: Use the first-linear polarization formula to derive inner-product preservation from norm preservation.
Use adjoint existence and pairing nondegeneracy for V†V=I; prove VV†=I from surjectivity without a choice axiom.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information (2018), Theorem 2.22
John Preskill, Quantum Computation, Chapter 3, §3.3.2

items.title: Unitary conjugation map
items.statement:
Let $H,K$ be nonzero finite-dimensional (have finite bases by [[def-dimension]])
complex inner-product spaces of equal
dimension. We call a surjective linear isometry
$U:H\to K$ ([[def-linear-isometry-and-orthogonal-or-unitary-operator]]) a
**unitary map** between these spaces. By
[[lem-qc-linear-isometry-adjoint-identities]], its adjoint exists uniquely,
$U^\dagger U=I_H$, and $UU^\dagger=I_K$. Define the
**unitary conjugation map**
$$\operatorname{Ad}_U:\mathcal L(H)\to\mathcal L(K),\qquad \operatorname{Ad}_U(X)=UXU^\dagger.$$ 
Here $\mathcal L(H)$ and $\mathcal L(K)$ are the complex-linear endomorphism
spaces ([[def-linear-map]]). It is well-defined because the composition is
$U\circ X\circ U^\dagger:K\to K$, and it is complex-linear in $X$.
proof_obligations: Specify a surjective linear isometry U:H→K and the domains of U and U†.
Define Ad_U on the full operator spaces and state the channel property as a separate proposition.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information (2018), §2.2.1

items.title: Trace preservation is Kraus normalization
items.statement:
Let $H,K$ be finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces and let
$\Phi(X)=\sum_{a\in A}K_aXK_a^\dagger$ be a finite Kraus representation,
where each $K_a:H\to K$. The map $\Phi$ is trace-preserving on all of
$\mathcal L(H)$, meaning $\operatorname{tr}_K(\Phi(X))=\operatorname{tr}_H(X)$
for every $X\in\mathcal L(H)$, if and only if
$$\sum_{a\in A}K_a^\dagger K_a=I_H.$$
proof_obligations: Expand the trace of the Kraus sum and cycle compatible rectangular products.
Use the nondegenerate trace pairing for the converse on all input operators, including dimension zero.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information (2018), Theorem 2.26
John Preskill, Quantum Computation, Chapter 3, §3.2.1

items.title: Unitary conjugation is invariant under a global phase
items.statement:
Let $H,K$ be nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces of equal
dimension, let $U:H\to K$ be a unitary map, and let $z\in\mathbb C$ satisfy
$|z|=1$. Then $zU$ is unitary and
$$\operatorname{Ad}_{zU}=\operatorname{Ad}_{U}.$$
This equality concerns conjugation by a single unitary. It makes no assertion
about controlled uses, where a scalar on one control branch may be a relative
phase.
proof_obligations: Prove zU remains surjective and norm-preserving when |z|=1.
Compute conjugation on every operator and state why this does not settle a controlled use.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information (2018), §2.2.1
John Preskill, Quantum Computation, Chapter 3, §3.2.1

items.title: Choi matrix with input factor first
items.statement:
Let $H_{\mathrm{in}}$ and $H_{\mathrm{out}}$ be finite-dimensional (have
finite bases by [[def-dimension]]) complex inner-product spaces
([[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]), and fix an
ordered orthonormal basis $\mathcal B=(e_0,\ldots,e_{n-1})$ of
$H_{\mathrm{in}}$ (the register basis convention is in
[[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]]). For $i,j<n$, let
$E_{ij}\in\mathcal L(H_{\mathrm{in}})$ be the matrix unit, where
$\mathcal L(H_{\mathrm{in}})$ denotes the complex-linear endomorphisms
([[def-linear-map]]),
$E_{ij}x:=\langle x,e_j\rangle e_i$, using the root inner product convention
that the first argument is linear. Given a complex-linear map
$\Phi:\mathcal L(H_{\mathrm{in}})\to\mathcal L(H_{\mathrm{out}})$
([[def-linear-map]]), its **Choi matrix relative to $\mathcal B$** is

$$J_{\mathcal B}(\Phi):=\sum_{i,j<n} E_{ij}\otimes\Phi(E_{ij})\in\mathcal L(H_{\mathrm{in}}\otimes H_{\mathrm{out}}),$$
where the operator tensor is the tensor map of [[def-qc-tensor-map]] and the
tensor inner product is the finite product pairing in
[[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]].

The tensor factors are ordered input first and output second. The coordinate
matrix has size $(n\,\dim H_{\mathrm{out}})\times(n\,\dim H_{\mathrm{out}})$.
The chosen input basis is part of this definition. If the input basis is
empty, the displayed sum is empty; if $\dim H_{\mathrm{out}}=0$, each
summand is zero and $J_{\mathcal B}(\Phi)$ is the unique endomorphism of the
zero-dimensional tensor product.
proof_obligations: Fix the ordered input basis and input-first/output-second factor order.
Define matrix units in the first-linear root convention and state the finite matrix size and zero cases.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information (2018), §2.2.1–2.2.2
John Preskill, Quantum Computation, Chapter 3, §§3.3.1–3.3.2

items.title: Isometric Stinespring representation
items.statement:
Let $H$, $K$, and $E$ be finite-dimensional (have finite bases by
[[def-dimension]]) complex inner-product spaces
([[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]), and let
$V:H\to K\otimes E$ be a linear isometry
([[def-linear-isometry-and-orthogonal-or-unitary-operator]]), so
$V^\dagger V=I_H$ by [[lem-qc-linear-isometry-adjoint-identities]]. The map

$$\Phi_V(X):=\operatorname{Tr}_E(VXV^\dagger),\qquad X\in\mathcal L(H),$$

is the **isometric Stinespring form** associated with $V$. An **isometric
Stinespring representation** ([[def-linear-map]]) of
$\Phi:\mathcal L(H)\to\mathcal L(K)$ is such a formula, where
$\operatorname{Tr}_E$ is the finite partial trace
([[def-qc-partial-trace]]) under the tensor convention
[[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]], together with its chosen finite
environment $E$ and isometry $V$. The composition
$V\circ X\circ V^\dagger$ is an endomorphism of $K\otimes E$, and the
partial trace maps it linearly to an endomorphism of $K$. Thus the displayed
formula defines a complex-linear map on the full input operator space. This
definition makes no existence assertion for an arbitrary map.
proof_obligations: Define the finite environment and partial-trace formula with K first and E second.
Separate definition of the form from universal existence and the channel property.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information (2018), §2.2.1–2.2.3
John Preskill, Quantum Computation, Chapter 3, §3.3.2

items.title: Tensor products of operator matrix units form a basis
items.statement:
Let $H,H'$ be finite-dimensional (have finite bases by [[def-dimension]])
complex inner-product spaces with ordered
orthonormal bases $(e_u)_{u<n}$ and $(f_s)_{s<m}$. For $u,v<n$ and $s,t<m$
define $E_{uv}x:=\langle x,e_v\rangle e_u$ and
$F_{st}y:=\langle y,f_t\rangle f_s$. Then
$(E_{uv}\otimes F_{st})_{u,v,s,t}$ is a basis of
$\mathcal L(H\otimes H')$. Empty dimensions give the empty basis of the zero
endomorphism space. The root pairing is linear in its first argument, so the
displayed matrix-unit maps are linear.
proof_obligations: Compute each tensor matrix unit on the ordered product basis.
Use coordinate columns for spanning and uniqueness, including zero factors.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information (2018), §2.2.2
John Preskill, Quantum Computation, Chapter 3, §3.2.1

items.title: A positive Choi matrix yields finite Kraus operators
items.statement:
Let $H,K$ be finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces, let
$\mathcal B=(e_i)_{i<n}$ be an ordered orthonormal basis of $H$, and let
$\Phi:\mathcal L(H)\to\mathcal L(K)$ be complex-linear. If
$J_{\mathcal B}(\Phi)$ is non-negative, then $\Phi$ has a finite Kraus
representation with at most $\dim(H)\dim(K)$ operators.
proof_obligations: Use a positive square root and its finite orthonormal eigenbasis to construct rectangular Kraus maps.
Verify every input-first Choi matrix-unit entry and handle zero spaces and the zero Choi operator.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information (2018), §2.2.2
John Preskill, Quantum Computation, Chapter 3, §§3.3.1–3.3.2

items.title: Finite-dimensional quantum channel
items.statement:
Let $H$ and $K$ be finite-dimensional (have finite bases by [[def-dimension]])
complex inner-product spaces. A
**quantum channel** from $H$ to $K$ is a complex-linear map
$\Phi:\mathcal L(H)\to\mathcal L(K)$ ([[def-linear-map]]) that is completely
positive ([[def-qc-completely-positive-map]]) and trace-preserving, meaning

$$\operatorname{tr}(\Phi(X))=\operatorname{tr}(X)\qquad\text{for every }X\in\mathcal L(H),$$

where trace is the basis-independent trace of a finite-dimensional
endomorphism ([[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]). Trace preservation is
required on the full operator space, not only on density operators. This
definition is mathematical and assumes no physical realization.
proof_obligations: Specify finite input/output spaces and trace preservation on the full operator space.
State that no physical realization is assumed.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information (2018), §2.2.1
John Preskill, Quantum Computation, Chapter 3, §§3.2.1 and 3.2.6

items.title: Complete positivity implies Choi positivity
items.statement:
Let $H$ and $K$ be finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces, fix an
ordered orthonormal basis $\mathcal B$ of $H$, and let
$\Phi:\mathcal L(H)\to\mathcal L(K)$ be completely positive. Then
$J_{\mathcal B}(\Phi)$ is non-negative.
proof_obligations: Apply the defining block amplification to a positive rank-one operator on H tensor C^n.
Swap the amplified output/reference factors explicitly to reach the input-first Choi order; include zero spaces.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information (2018), §2.2.2
John Preskill, Quantum Computation, Chapter 3, §§3.2.6 and 3.3.1

items.title: A finite Kraus sum is completely positive
items.statement:
Let $H,K$ be finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces and let
$\Phi:\mathcal L(H)\to\mathcal L(K)$ have a finite Kraus representation
$\Phi(X)=\sum_{a\in A}K_a X K_a^\dagger$. Then $\Phi$ is completely positive.
proof_obligations: Show every finite block amplification agrees with the Kraus sum on product matrix units.
Show each operator conjugation and its finite sum preserves non-negativity, including an empty family.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information (2018), §2.2.2
John Preskill, Quantum Computation, Chapter 3, §§3.2.1 and 3.2.6

items.title: An isometry followed by partial trace is a channel
items.statement:
Let $H,K,E$ be finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces and let
$V:H\to K\otimes E$ be a linear isometry. Then
$$\Phi(X)=\operatorname{Tr}_E(VXV^\dagger),\qquad X\in\mathcal L(H),$$
is a quantum channel from $H$ to $K$.
proof_obligations: Express partial trace as a finite Kraus sum using environment coordinate blocks.
Compose that Kraus family with the isometry and use V†V=I to prove trace preservation.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information (2018), §2.2.2
John Preskill, Quantum Computation, Chapter 3, §3.3.2

items.title: Kraus and Choi characterizations of complete positivity
items.statement:
Let $H,K$ be finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces, fix an ordered
orthonormal basis $\mathcal B$ of $H$, and let
$\Phi:\mathcal L(H)\to\mathcal L(K)$ be complex-linear. The following are
equivalent: $\Phi$ is completely positive; $J_{\mathcal B}(\Phi)$ is
non-negative; and $\Phi$ has a finite Kraus representation.
proof_obligations: Assemble CP to Choi non-negativity, positive Choi to a finite Kraus representation, and Kraus to CP from the separate proofs.
Keep one fixed input basis and the stated Choi factor order in every direction.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information (2018), §2.2.2
John Preskill, Quantum Computation, Chapter 3, §§3.2.6 and 3.3.1–3.3.2

items.title: Unitary conjugation is a channel
items.statement:
Let $H,K$ be nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces and let
$U:H\to K$ be a unitary map. Then $\operatorname{Ad}_U$ is a channel. For
any nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space $L$ and unitary
map $V:K\to L$,
$\operatorname{Ad}_{VU}=\operatorname{Ad}_V\circ\operatorname{Ad}_U$; the
inverse channel to $\operatorname{Ad}_U$ is $\operatorname{Ad}_{U^\dagger}$.
proof_obligations: Use the one-element Kraus family U to prove complete positivity and trace preservation.
Check composition and inverse as typed identities on every input operator.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information (2018), §2.2.1

items.title: Finite-dimensional channels compose and tensor
items.statement:
Let $\Phi:\mathcal L(H)\to\mathcal L(K)$ and
$\Psi:\mathcal L(K)\to\mathcal L(L)$ be finite-dimensional quantum channels.
Then $\Psi\circ\Phi$ is a channel. If
$\Theta:\mathcal L(H')\to\mathcal L(K')$ is another finite-dimensional
channel, the tensor map
$\Phi\otimes\Theta:\mathcal L(H\otimes H')\to\mathcal L(K\otimes K')$
is the linear map specified on product matrix units by
$(\Phi\otimes\Theta)(E_{uv}\otimes F_{st})=
\Phi(E_{uv})\otimes\Theta(F_{st})$. The basis result
[[lem-qc-tensor-products-of-operator-matrix-units-form-a-basis]] makes this
map well-defined and unique. It is also a channel, with the displayed factor
order.
proof_obligations: Construct Kraus families for composition and tensor maps and verify their actions on every input.
Prove complete positivity and normalization, using the product matrix-unit basis to define the tensor map.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information (2018), §§2.2.1–2.2.3
John Preskill, Quantum Computation, Chapter 3, §§3.2–3.3

items.title: The Choi partial trace characterizes trace preservation
items.statement:
Let $H,K$ be finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces, fix an ordered
orthonormal basis $\mathcal B=(e_i)_{i<n}$ of $H$, and let
$\Phi:\mathcal L(H)\to\mathcal L(K)$ be completely positive. Then
$\operatorname{tr}_K(\Phi(X))=\operatorname{tr}_H(X)$ for every
$X\in\mathcal L(H)$ if and only if
$$\operatorname{Tr}_K J_{\mathcal B}(\Phi)=I_H,$$
where $\operatorname{Tr}_K$ is the partial trace over the output factor in the
input-first/output-second Choi convention.
proof_obligations: Compute the output partial-trace coefficient (i,j) as S_ji in the fixed product basis.
Use the all-operator Kraus normalization theorem in both directions and check zero input/output cases.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information (2018), Theorem 2.26 and Corollary 2.27
John Preskill, Quantum Computation, Chapter 3, §§3.2.6 and 3.3.1

items.title: Every finite-dimensional channel has a finite isometric dilation
items.statement:
Let $H,K$ be finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces and let
$\Phi:\mathcal L(H)\to\mathcal L(K)$ be a quantum channel. It has a finite
Kraus representation, and for any chosen such representation with $N$
operators $K_a:H\to K$ there are an $N$-dimensional environment $E$ and a
linear isometry $V:H\to K\otimes E$ such that
$$\Phi(X)=\operatorname{Tr}_E(VXV^\dagger)\quad\text{for every }X\in\mathcal L(H).$$
proof_obligations: For any chosen finite Kraus family construct Vx=Σa K_ax tensor u_a and prove it is an isometry.
Compute the partial trace in the product basis and recover the given map, including the empty environment case.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information (2018), Theorem 2.22
John Preskill, Quantum Computation, Chapter 3, §3.3.2

items.title: Finite channel, Kraus, Choi, and Stinespring equivalence
items.statement:
Let $H,K$ be finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces, fix an ordered
orthonormal basis $\mathcal B$ of $H$, and let
$\Phi:\mathcal L(H)\to\mathcal L(K)$ be complex-linear. The following four
conditions are equivalent:

1. $\Phi$ is a quantum channel.
2. $J_{\mathcal B}(\Phi)\succeq0$ and
   $\operatorname{Tr}_KJ_{\mathcal B}(\Phi)=I_H$.
3. $\Phi(X)=\sum_aK_aXK_a^\dagger$ for a finite family of maps
$K_a:H\to K$ with
   $\sum_aK_a^\dagger K_a=I_H$.
4. There are a finite-dimensional $E$ and an isometry $V:H\to K\otimes E$
   with $\Phi(X)=\operatorname{Tr}_E(VXV^\dagger)$ for every $X$.

The Choi order is input factor first, output factor second.
proof_obligations: Assemble only the preceding proved implications and make each direction explicit.
Track the fixed Choi basis, factor order, Kraus domains, and environment order without circular dependencies.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information (2018), §§2.2.2–2.2.3
John Preskill, Quantum Computation, Chapter 3, §§3.2.6–3.3.2

title: Channels, Kraus, Choi, and Stinespring Representations — Examples

items.title: Qubit dephasing channel in Kraus and Choi forms
items.statement:
Let $H=\mathbb C^2$ with standard basis $e_0,e_1$, let $0\le p\le1$, and
put $Z=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}$,
$K_0=\sqrt p\,I$, and $K_1=\sqrt{1-p}\,Z$, using the nonnegative real
square roots. For $\Phi(X)=K_0XK_0^\dagger+K_1XK_1^\dagger$, compute the
Kraus normalization, the action on a density matrix, and the Choi matrix in
the input-first/output-second convention. The map is a phase-flip family;
at $p=1/2$ it is the completely dephasing channel.
proof_obligations: Compute the Kraus normalization, action on an arbitrary density operator, and the input-first Choi matrix explicitly.
Check the Choi eigenvalues and output partial trace, including p=0, p=1, and p=1/2.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information (2018), §2.2.3
John Preskill, Quantum Computation, Chapter 3, §3.4.2
